## Summary

A quote-tweet disagreement in its purest form. @InvestingAddict posts the Bogleheads classic — *"Nobody ever regrets investing in the S&P 500. Many regret trying to outperform it."* — the regret-asymmetry argument for indexing. The Momentum Investor counters with a confident dual claim: **100+ strategies in hand that beat $SPY**, requiring only **one portfolio adjustment a year**, delivering a **consistent 2–5% annual edge**.

Nothing is disclosed — no rules, no equity curves, no links. The claim is unfalsifiable as posted.

## Why it matters

- **"100+ strategies" is the overfitting tell, not the strength it sounds like.** If a hundred distinct rule-sets all post the same edge on the same history, they are almost certainly a hundred re-skinnings of one or two underlying factor exposures mined from the same window. A genuine edge is rare; a *zoo* of edges is the signature of data mining. "Consistently" is the load-bearing word, and edge decay is exactly what [[2026-09-16-guirao-breakout-decay-2026]] documents.
- **The base rate is the quoted tweet's strongest card.** SPIVA-style scorecards show the large majority of professional active managers underperform the S&P 500 over 15–20yr windows — managers with more than annual rebalancing and more than 100 strategies at their disposal. "Adjust once a year and beat SPY by 2–5%" is a claim about beating people who spend their careers trying.
- **Internal irony: momentum doesn't survive annual rebalancing.** Momentum as a factor decays on the order of weeks-to-months; a genuinely annual rebalance harvests almost none of it. A momentum-branded account advertising yearly adjustments is either not really running momentum (a value/quality/small-cap tilt wearing the label — the classic Fama-French way to "beat SPY" over long windows) or harvesting a different premium than the brand implies. Either way the label and the mechanism don't match.
- **Plausibility calibration against our own captures:** the one fully-disclosed TAA system in the vault ([[2026-09-09-p123-five-etf-rotation]]) earned ~2.6pp/yr annualized (9.74% vs 7.14%) *against a 60/40 benchmark — not SPY —* over 28 years with the full stats card attached. An anonymous "2–5% over SPY, consistently" is claiming more edge with zero disclosure.
- **Why it's in the vault anyway:** this is the cleanest one-tweet statement of the two poles the whole strategy-capture cluster lives between. Our replication queue ([[2026-09-13-cointradernik-regime-rotation-rr-pro]] with its disclosed IS→OOS Sharpe decay, [[2026-08-29-milk-man-replication-metrics]]) is the "you can beat SPY" pole; the quoted tweet is the standing caution that in-sample edges decay out-of-sample. Calibration anchor for how much weight any single backtest stat deserves — including the ones we capture sympathetically.
- **Skepticism gates:** zero disclosure means zero replication candidates; reference only, no task. Practitioner honesty contrast: [[2026-10-01-momentmal-trend-following-us-markets]] is what a momentum practitioner sounds like when naming where the style *doesn't* work.
